text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- British Prime Minister Tony Blair wants Swedish cooperation in the European Union (EU) he wrote in a comment.
- The ruling Social Democrats decision to let Sweden remain outside Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) at the start in 1999 will not affect households' economies immediately.
- Fewer companies and persons filed for bankruptcy in May with the number of company bankruptcies falling by 23 percent to 647 from the same month a year earlier.

- Employment in Sweden is at its lowest levels since 1974 despite growing Gross Domestic Product while the average working year has increased by two to three weeks over the past four years. This increase in working hours corresponds to up to 300,000 jobs, according to Statistics Sweden.
- Property company Nackebro has made a counter bid for Fabege, offering shareholders 85 crowns a share which is 14 percent higher than a bid from rival property firm Hufvudstaden.
- Volvo's new car registrations in Japan plunged by 38.8 percent in May compared to the same period a year ago to 1,463 cars.

- LE Lundberg Foretagen AB, a large Swedish real estate and asset management company, announced that it has asked to be removed from the primary A list of the Stockholm Stock Exchange. The company's stock will instead be traded from June 9 on the smaller O list. The reason for the move is a new law adopted by parliament last week that forces the owners of family-owned firms traded on the Stockholm Exchange's primary list to pay a higher wealth tax.

- Property company Nackebro has placed a cash bid worth 2.2 billion crowns on competing property company Fabege . The offer of 85 crowns a share is a counter-bid to a previous offer by real estate firm Hufvudstaden which was much lower.

- Spray Interactive Media Agency AB, one of Sweden's fastest growing Internet companies, plans to raise 30 million crowns with a directed share issue. About 20 percent of Spray will be sold which means the total company is valued at about 150 million crowns.
